title: Adaptive upgrade fencing: micro-wave rollouts for heterogeneous GPU pools
creator: Arjun Patel
description: Problem statement: Upgrades to GPU pools (driver/runtime/kernel changes and new runtime kernels) currently cause brief capacity churn that triggers autoscaler activity and tenant QoS regressions. Existing drain-based approaches either create large eviction waves or require long maintenance windows. Goal: implement an "adaptive upgrade fence" that enables micro-wave rollouts (tiny, tenant-aware waves across heterogeneous GPU devices) that preserve burst capacity, coordinate with autoscalers via a lease handshake, and provide safe fast rollback.
acceptance_criteria: No end-user requests should observe >3% increase in tail latency (p95) attributable to upgrade activity during a rollout in staging and less than 2% in canary production.
Cluster autoscaler must not trigger more than one scale-out event caused by upgrade traffic per pool during a controlled rollout window.
Ability to complete a full pool upgrade with <2% sustained capacity reduction for any 10-minute window across affected pools.
Automated rollback triggers on: (a) sustained p95 latency degradation >10% for 5 minutes; (b) admission rejections rate >0.5% for 5 minutes; (c) increased error-rate in model-serving >1%.
E2E test harness (simulated tenanted traffic) validates upgrade fencing across at least three heterogeneous GPU types and passes within CI pipeline.
Migration runbook updated and validated by SRE and PM owners with a signed-off checklist.
technical_notes: Introduce a 'fence token' lease API that upgrade controller acquires per pool slice to reserve a soft buffer of capacity (configurable percentage).

Micro-wave concept: break pool into N micro-waves by tenant affinity and device heterogeneity; each wave size is computed by admission pressure and historical burst metric (default target 1-2% of active capacity).

Autoscaler handshake: before draining nodes in a micro-wave, send 'pre-drain' signal to autoscaler; autoscaler replies with 'accept' and provides expected fill/scale budget; controller waits or reduces wave size if budget insufficient.

Eviction policy: prefer soft-drain preferring synthetic job reroute, KV cache warmup reuse across wave neighbors, and avoid complete model reloads by routing to compatible model-quantization variants during short drains.
Implement circuit-breaker for model-variant fallback: if new runtime fails compatibility checks, route matching requests to prior binary with automatic weight ramp-down.
Expose observability: per-wave telemetry (wave_id, start_ts, end_ts, evicted_pods, admission_rejections, autoscaler_signals) to Grafana and tracing.
Control plane config: release channels annotated on pools (lts-stable, lts-candidate, edge) to allow staged gating and per-channel grace windows.
Add integration test that simulates autoscaler suppression signal and verifies controller reduces wave pacing and honors lease TTL.
Backward compatibility: fencing API graceful-fallback for older controllers that don't support lease semantics (degrades to conservative waves).
rollout_plan: Implement lease API and autoscaler acceptance endpoint (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4897).
Add micro-wave slicing algorithm and per-tenant affinity classifier (internal RFC linked in docs).
Run staging campaign: run 50 controlled micro-wave upgrades across staging pools with traffic replay and validate acceptance criteria.
Canary in production: pick two low-traffic dedicated pools, apply fencing with conservative buffer (3%), monitor for 24 hours.
Gradual ramp: increase parallelism and reduce buffer over 5 rolling days if metrics stable; full rollout only after SRE sign-off.
Post-upgrade verification: run smoke tests, validate KV cache hit ratios, and ensure no admission rejections spike.
If rollback trigger hits, automated controller aborts further waves and invokes rollback plan that reverts node image and re-balances traffic.
monitoring_playbook: Primary dashboards: grafana/redwood/upgrade-fencing-overview (p50/p95/p99 latency by customer, admission_rejections, autoscaler_events).
Alerting: page SRE on sustained p95 degradation >10% for 5 minutes or admission rejection rate >0.5% for 5 minutes.

Runbook steps: 1) Pause controller; 2) Acquire autoscaler manual lock; 3) Disable new wave scheduling; 4) If needed, trigger rollback job with target image set to previous runtime; 5) Notify customers via status page if degradation persists >30 minutes.
Post-incident log collection: collect per-wave traces, node-level GPU metrics, kernel logs, and controller debug output for 1 hour post-failure.
